function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact spot price of gold for today.  The most reliable way to get the current U.S. gold price is to check a reputable financial news or commodities site that updates in real time, such as:

| Source | Typical update frequency | How to access |
|--------|--------------------------|---------------|
| **Kitco** | Every minute | https://www.kitco.com/ |
| **Bloomberg** | Every minute | https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/commodities |
| **Reuters** | Every minute | https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities |
| **London Bullion Market Association (LBMA)** | Every minute | https://www.lbma.org.uk/ |
| **U.S. Treasury / Federal Reserve** | Daily | https://home.treasury.gov/ |

If you need the price for a specific time (e.g., closing price on a particular day), most of these sites also provide historical charts and daily summaries.  

**Quick tip:** On most of these sites, the spot price is shown in U.S. dollars per troy ounce. If you’re looking for the price in a different currency, you can usually toggle the currency or use a quick conversion tool.
